title: Fanout
explain: Fanout is one input turning into many outputs, and the name covers two different problems. In the delivery model the question is who gets a change: copy it to every follower when it is written, or merge at read time. In the request model one request calls many downstreams, and I first ask if the fanout can be avoided, then bound what is left.
model:
**Delivery model: who gets this change?** Hand one change to many people.

- **Fanout-on-write (push):** at post time, write a reference into each follower's inbox. Reads are one lookup; a write costs F writes and storage.
- **Fanout-on-read (pull):** store the post once; each reader merges the posts of everyone they follow. Writes are cheap; a read costs one lookup per followee.
- **Hybrid:** push for ordinary authors; for a celebrity, switch to fanout-on-read and merge their posts in at read time.

**Request model: fanout to downstreams.** First make it *not* a fanout; if it cannot be avoided, shape it by size:

| Fan degree | Approach |
|---|---|
| ~100 vendors | batch, per-host connection pools |
| ~100k vendors | filter / match / ML / precompute who matters |
| 1 job to 1M tasks that all must run | lazy loading + batching: a page at a time, like a generator |

**Lazy expansion:** turn the job into tasks page by page; push to the queue only while below a watermark; load the next page when it drains. Reads, writes and queue size never spike.

details.q: When do you pick fanout-on-write and when fanout-on-read?
details.a: Do the work where it is rarer. An ordinary user with 200 followers who posts once a day, read by followers 50 times a day: 200 writes per post against 10,000 reads, so push. A celebrity with 20 M followers is the opposite: push is a write storm, so pull.

20,000,000 inbox writes at a sustained 50,000 per second take 400 s, nearly seven minutes during which followers see the post at wildly different times and the inbox store is saturated for everyone else. Hence the hybrid: skip the push for celebrities.

details.q: What does a hybrid feed read actually do?
details.a: Read the precomputed inbox (pushed posts from ordinary authors), fetch recent posts from the few celebrities this user follows, and merge by time. Push covers the many cheaply; pull is bounded because the set of celebrities per user is small.

details.q: A job must create 1,000,000 tasks and every one must run. Why not insert them all at once?
details.a: It causes a read/write spike and a huge queue backlog. The work is unavoidable but its shape is not: keep the job as a compact description plus a [cursor](#/sd/f/cursor), create a page of tasks, enqueue while below the high watermark, and create the next page when the queue drains.

details.q: A new job should notify matching vendors out of 100,000 registered. The first design calls everyone and lets them filter. Better?
details.a: Match first (region, category, capacity, a precomputed index or a model) and call only those that qualify. Above about a hundred targets brute force is a cost and a risk; shrinking the set beats making each call faster.

details.q: When fanout to about 100 vendors cannot be avoided, what do you do?
details.a: Batch where the vendor allows it, use per-host [connection pools](#/sd/f/connection-pooling) so you do not open 100 connections per request, bound concurrency, and give each call its own timeout. Then apply the [caller diligence](#/sd/f/caller-diligence) checks to each leg.

details.q: What does fanout-on-write cost besides the write count?
details.a: Storage per follower, work for new followers (backfill their inbox), and unfollow/delete handling. Fanout-on-read costs merge latency and repeated work per read, which caching can reduce.

prompts.q: Compare fanout-on-write and fanout-on-read, and say when you pick each.
points: Push: copy into each inbox at write, cheap reads
Pull: store once, merge at read, cheap writes
Decide by read/write ratio and fan degree

prompts.q: Design a news feed that handles celebrities.
points: Push for ordinary authors into per-user inboxes
Celebrities pulled at read time and merged by time
Numbers: 20 M followers at 50k writes/s is 400 s

prompts.q: One job fans out to 1M tasks. How do you keep load flat?
points: Store the job as a description with a cursor
Materialise tasks a page at a time, like a generator
Enqueue only below a high watermark; refill on drain
Batch and bound the downstream calls
Ask first whether all tasks are needed (filter or match)
